title: An FPRAS for Cell-Bounded Contingency Tables
main_claim: Theorem 1.1: there is an FPRAS, using only fair coin flips, for counting nonnegative integer m×n matrices with given row sums, column sums and per-cell upper bounds, with all data in binary and both dimensions varying. Its bit cost is polynomial in L, 1/ε and log(1/δ) on every execution, and it outputs 0 on infeasible inputs.
coverage:
I read Sections 1–7 in full (scales, integer-signatures, signatures, transport, evaluation, algorithm). I did not audit Section 8 (network-flow corollaries) or the history section. Hand-verified steps:
(1) Forest lemma constants: |Δz_t| ≤ 4d·b_t, Σ|δ| ≤ 2dW, D ≤ H, Lipschitz constant 2Ad².
(2) Integer balanced-summation lemma: the laminar rank-one identity telescopes; the M=1 null-axis case holds; for M≥2 I re-derived the axis products u_{k-1}(g_k−g_{k-1}) and u_{k+1}(g_{k+1}−g_k), the cancellation to a^T V_k a + 2u_k g_k² − u_{k-1}g_{k-1}² − u_{k+1}g_{k+1}² ≤ 0, and the telescoping sum.
(3) Corollary 3.2 laminar model, and tree-marginal log-concavity, including the limit order α→0. A Python brute force over about 3000 random small instances found no log-concavity violation in single-cell marginals.
(4) Contamination arithmetic: far assignments have mass ≤ 2^{-3K}; near violations have mass fraction ≤ 4dγK = ε/128; together C(H) ≤ (1+ε/32)Z.
(5) Lift comparison bounds (x+1)(y+1) and 1/(xy) stay within [W^{-2}, W^2]; the omission property of f and the addition property of f̃ follow by group decomposition and factorial cancellation; the cubic-contraction Perron argument holds; the entries N_ll, N_ik, N_il, N_lk of the 3×3 matrix and the Schur-complement bound give the two-pair and three-pair defect inequalities.
(6) One-hole transport: the matrix N, h^T N d = −2X, d^T N d = −2u, the potential increment 2X²/(uW_t), level additivity, the root value −2v_t/(s_0 s_1), and the leaf divergence cancellation.
(7) Sink existence; v_t/W_t ≤ 4q² z_σ; C_p = p(1+8pq²); the defect-mean setup with s_0 = c_il and v_t ≤ c_it; C_d = 8+32pq³; K_obs; the time-average and trace (Kac formula) bounds.
(8) Bin evaluator: density comparison [V/4, 2V], T ∈ [1/8, 4], the telescoping identity, the Prékopa–Leindler conductance bound 1/(1024d²B), walk length, and the rounding range β ∈ [−2, 2].
(9) Annealing: closed forms for the initial defect brackets (b+1, 1, (b+1)(b+2)/6, (b+1)/6) and the multipliers 6 and 6(b_i+1)/(b_l+2); warm-start domination 2^M·e^{−2(M+5)} < 1; cap and empirical-error union bounds; multiplier goodness carried through the induction; coupling budget 10J_*ξ = η/100; final log error ≤ ε/16; median amplification constant (5/(4√2))^10 < 1/2.
sibling_notes: The family-115 board was empty when I checked. The paper says it adapts the common-bases construction (OpenAICommonBases2026, Sections 4–6) and the laminar summation lemma (OpenAIExactTables2026, Lemmas 3.2–3.4). Both are re-proved inline here, so there is no circular dependence on those companion papers.
